mainTopic: Found loan documents: רב אסי, אביי (עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו), and how שמואל explains our משנה
overview: The עמוד opens with the end of רב אסי's answer. A scribe may write a loan document for a borrower without the lender present only if it is a שטר הקנאה, where the borrower ties his land to the debt from the written date. The גמרא challenges him from our משנה, which refuses to return a found document with אחריות נכסים because it may be dated before the real loan. רב אסי answers that a lost document has become less trustworthy. אביי gives a different reason: עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו, meaning the witnesses' signatures acquire the lien for the lender even in an ordinary document. The גמרא limits this to documents that actually reached the recipient. It then explains that for אביי our משנה worries about repayment and a scheme (פרעון וקנוניא). For שמואל, who does not share that worry, the משנה is about a borrower who denies the debt. A document without a guarantee is still returned, because following רבי מאיר it collects nothing and is only paper to cover the lender's flask. The גמרא then asks why the paper should not go to the borrower instead, and the answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: רב אסי: the case is about deeds of transfer
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי finishes his answer. The משנה that allows writing a document for the borrower without the lender present is talking about שטרי הקנאה, where the borrower tied his property to the debt from the date written.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about deeds of transfer, because the borrower already obligated himself from that date.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of רב אסי's answer to an earlier question. He says the document in question is a special kind, a שטר הקנאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that a document dated before the actual loan would let the lender take land from buyers unfairly. In a שטר הקנאה the borrower agrees that his property is tied to the debt from the date written, even before he gets the money. So an early date causes no unfairness.

keyTerms.meaning: Deeds of transfer: documents in which the borrower ties his property to the debt from the date written
He obligated himself (created a lien on his property)
Because / since

phrases.english: It is talking about deeds of transfer,
since he has obligated himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אסי's answer to the earlier challenge, which comes before this text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific kind of document (שטר הקנאה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing a document without the lender present seems risky, because the loan might happen later than the date written.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a שטר הקנאה the lien starts at the written date anyway, so there is no unfairness to buyers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up רב אסי's position, which the rest of the text tests against our משנה.

steps.title: Challenge from our משנה about not returning found documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אסי from our משנה. That משנה says a found document with אחריות נכסים is not returned, out of concern that it was written in ניסן but the loan only happened in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at our משנה, which teaches: 'If the documents include a property guarantee, he should not return them.' We explained this as a case where the borrower admits the debt. The reason is the worry that maybe he wrote it to borrow in ניסן, did not borrow until תשרי, and the lender will come to take land from buyers unfairly. Why should he not return it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings our משנה as a challenge to רב אסי. Our משנה worries about a document dated earlier than the actual loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה refuses to return a found document even when the borrower admits he owes. The only reason left is the worry about an early date. If רב אסי says such early-dated documents are not a problem, our משנה's worry seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge)
A property guarantee: the debt can be collected from the borrower's land
We established / we explained (the case as)
To take land away from buyers
Unlawfully

steps.confusionAlert: The borrower here admits he owes the money, so the worry is not about a fake debt. The worry is only about buyers who bought land between the written date and the real loan date.

phrases.english: If so, our Mishnah, which teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים לֹא יַחֲזִיר״,
phrases.english: 'If they include a property guarantee, he should not return them,'
and we established it as a case where the debtor admits,
and the reason is that perhaps he wrote it to borrow in Nisan
but did not borrow until Tishrei,
and he will come to seize property from buyers unlawfully,
why should he not return it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אסי's answer from Step 1 using our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that the early-date problem is solved by שטרי הקנאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה clearly worries about early-dated documents. רב אסי's approach seems to remove any reason for that worry.

steps.title: Spelling out the challenge: neither kind of document is a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both possibilities. A שטר הקנאה is fine because the lien starts at the written date. An ordinary document is never written without the lender present, so it cannot be dated early.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us see. If it is a deed of transfer, he obligated himself from that date! If it is a document that is not a deed of transfer, there is nothing to worry about, because you said that when the lender is not with him, we do not write it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the challenge by checking both kinds of documents. It shows that, according to רב אסי, neither kind should cause a worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: a שטר הקנאה, where an early date is no problem. Option two: an ordinary document, which according to רב אסי is never written unless the lender is present and the loan happens on the spot. Either way, our משנה's worry seems to disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see / let us examine
There is nothing to worry about
The lender
With him
We write

phrases.english: Let us see: if it is a deed of transfer,
he has obligated himself to him!
If it is a document that is not a deed of transfer,
there is nothing to worry about,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא אָמְרַתְּ כִּי לֵיכָּא מַלְוֶה בַּהֲדֵיהּ
phrases.english: since you said that when the lender is not with him,
phrases.notes: "You" means רב אסי. This is what his answer in Step 1 assumes.

phrases.english: we do not write it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the question in Step 2 is strong by covering both possible kinds of documents.
steps.kashyaTarget: The basis for our משנה's worry, according to רב אסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a two-sided trap. Whether the document is a שטר הקנאה or an ordinary one, there is no early-date risk, so our משנה should allow returning it.

steps.title: רב אסי: a lost document has lost its trustworthiness
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי agrees that ordinary documents are normally not written without the lender. But once a document has been lost, it becomes less trustworthy. So we worry it may have been written against the normal procedure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי could say to you: even though ordinary documents (not deeds of transfer) are not written when the lender is not present, in our משנה the document fell and was lost. That weakened it, and we worry that perhaps it just happened to be written that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers on behalf of רב אסי. A lost document is suspicious, so the usual assumption that proper procedure was followed no longer holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we trust that scribes followed the rule of writing an ordinary document only with the lender present. Losing the document weakens that trust, so we worry it may have been written outside the normal rules. So the two-sided challenge fails. The second option, an ordinary document, can still be worrying once it was lost.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (an answer given on someone's behalf)
Even though
It has been weakened / its trustworthiness is damaged
We worry / we are concerned
It happened to be written (by chance, not by the normal procedure)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אסי, an ordinary document is not written without the lender present, so normally there is no early-date worry. But a document that was lost is weakened, so we suspect it may have broken the rule. That is why the finder does not return it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea: losing a document can make it less trustworthy and remove the normal assumption that it was properly written.

phrases.english: Rav Asi could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּשְׁטָרֵי דְּלָאו הַקְנָאָה,
phrases.english: even though documents that are not deeds of transfer,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֵיכָּא מַלְוֶה בַּהֲדֵיהּ לָא כָּתְבִינַן,
phrases.english: when the lender is not with him, we do not write them,
in our Mishnah, since it fell, it has been weakened,
phrases.notes: "Fell" means the document was dropped and lost, which is why someone found it.

phrases.english: and we worry that perhaps it just happened to be written that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 2–3 by breaking its second side: the ordinary document.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a lost document versus a document still in normal hands
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ordinary documents are never written without the lender present, there is no early-date risk at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule holds in general, but a lost document has lost its trustworthiness, so we worry it broke the rule.

steps.title: אביי: the witnesses' signatures acquire for the lender
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a different answer than רב אסי. The witnesses' signatures acquire the lien for the lender, even in ordinary documents that are not שטרי הקנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the witnesses of the document, through their signatures, acquire on the lender's behalf. This is true even for documents that are not deeds of transfer.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a new way to explain the משנה that lets us write a document for the borrower without the lender there. He says the witnesses' signatures acquire for the lender, so the lien takes effect from the date written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי limited that משנה to שטרי הקנאה only. אביי does not need that limit. He holds that once the witnesses sign, they acquire the lien for the lender, so the written date is never really 'early' even for an ordinary loan document.

keyTerms.meaning: The document's witnesses, by signing it, acquire on the recipient's behalf
Ordinary documents that are not deeds of transfer
Acquiring something on another person's behalf

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing about the law of the משנה. He is giving a different reason why it is fine to write the document without the lender present.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Its witnesses, by their signatures, acquire for him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the lender. Once the witnesses sign, the lien on the borrower's property already belongs to the lender.

phrases.english: and even documents that are not deeds of transfer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: עֵדָיו בַּחֲתוּמָיו זָכִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב אסי's answer to the same question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative mechanism: the witnesses' signatures acquire the lien for the lender, so the date is not early.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a שטר הקנאה could be written without the lender, as רב אסי said.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any loan document may be written without the lender, because the witnesses acquire the lien for him.

steps.title: Why אביי did not accept Rav Asi's answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that אביי found רב אסי's answer difficult. If ordinary documents are never written without the lender, there is no reason to suspect a found document was written that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said this because רב אסי's answer was hard for him. Since you said we do not write ordinary documents when the lender is not present, there is no reason to worry that this one happened to be written that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what bothered אביי about רב אסי's approach, which is why he gave his own explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, רב אסי said that once a document is lost, we worry it was written against normal procedure. אביי finds this weak. If the rule is that such documents are not written without the lender, then losing the document should not make us suspect that the rule was broken.

keyTerms.meaning: It was difficult for him
Lender
It happened to be written (against normal procedure)

phrases.english: Because it was difficult for him:
phrases.notes: This explains why אביי did not simply accept רב אסי's answer.

phrases.english: Since you said that with documents that are not deeds of transfer

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֵיתֵיהּ לְמַלְוֶה בַּהֲדֵיהּ לָא כָּתְבִינַן,
phrases.english: when the lender is not with him, we do not write them,
there is no need to worry that it happened to be written that way.
phrases.notes: This pushes back on רב אסי's point in Step 4, that a lost document becomes less trustworthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind אביי's alternative in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's answer in Step 4, that a lost document may have been written against procedure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is that ordinary documents are never written without the lender, a lost document gives no real basis to suspect that the rule was broken.

steps.title: Challenge to אביי from found divorce documents and other documents
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says found גיטין, freedom documents, wills, gift deeds and receipts are not returned, because the writer may have changed his mind before giving them. But according to אביי, the witnesses already acquired for the recipient.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the משנה: if someone found divorce documents, freedom documents of slaves, wills, gift deeds or receipts, he should not return them. Perhaps they were written and then the writer changed his mind and decided not to give them. The גמרא asks: if he changed his mind, so what? Didn't you say the witnesses, by their signatures, acquire for the recipient?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה and uses it to attack אביי's rule that the witnesses' signatures acquire for the recipient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה worries that the writer changed his mind and never gave the document. If אביי is right that the signatures alone already acquire for the recipient, changing his mind should not matter, and the document should be returned to the recipient.

keyTerms.meaning: Divorce documents
Documents freeing slaves
Wills (written by someone who is ill)
Receipts showing a debt was paid
He reconsidered, changed his mind

phrases.english: But that which we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in this פרק, on דף 18a.

phrases.english: If he found divorce documents of women or freedom documents of slaves,
wills, gift deeds, or receipts,
he should not return them,
since perhaps they were written
and he changed his mind about them, deciding not to give them.
And if he changed his mind about them, what of it?
But didn't you say:
Its witnesses, by their signatures, acquire for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's rule from Step 5 using a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If signing alone acquires for the recipient, the writer changing his mind would not matter, yet the משנה treats it as a real concern.

steps.title: The signatures acquire only once the document reaches the recipient
steps.stepSummary: The rule that the witnesses acquire for the recipient applies only once the document came into his hands. If it never reached him, we do not say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This rule applies where the document reached his hand. But where it did not reach his hand, we do not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting אביי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the document is delivered, the signatures make the acquisition count from the time of signing. If the writer changed his mind and never delivered it, it never reached the recipient, so nothing was acquired. That is why the found documents in the משנה are not returned.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only in this case)
It reached his hand
We do not say (this rule)

steps.whatToRemember: עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו means the signatures make the document count from the date written, but only once it actually reaches the recipient. A document that was never delivered gives him nothing.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּקָא מָטוּ לִידֵיהּ.
phrases.english: These words apply where it reached his hand.
phrases.notes: 'His hand' means the person receiving the document, such as the lender, the wife or the slave.

phrases.english: But where it did not reach his hand,
we do not say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּקָא מָטוּ לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7 by limiting אביי's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule: it applies only after delivery.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The signatures alone acquire for the recipient even if he never receives the document.
steps.terutzMaskana: The signatures acquire only once the document reaches the recipient's hand, so an undelivered document gives him nothing.

steps.title: Bringing the משנה about found loan documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings our משנה, which says found loan documents with a property guarantee are not returned. It reminds us that we explained the reason as worry about a document dated ניסן for a loan made in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, look at our משנה: if someone found loan documents with a property guarantee, he should not return them. We explained that this is even when the borrower admits the debt. The reason is that maybe the document was written to borrow in ניסן, but the loan only happened in תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against אביי by quoting our משנה and the reason we gave for it earlier. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the borrower admits he owes the money, the finder should not return the document. That is because the date on it might be earlier than the real loan. Then the lender could wrongly take land from people who bought from the borrower between ניסן and תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan document
A property guarantee, meaning the lender can collect even from land the borrower later sold
We established it, meaning we explained which case the text is talking about
The borrower admits he owes the money

steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not that the debt is fake, because the borrower admits it. The worry is only about the date, which could hurt people who bought land from the borrower.

phrases.english: Rather, what about the משנה that teaches:
If he found loan documents,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶם אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים – לֹא יַחְזִיר.
phrases.english: if they include a property guarantee, he should not return them.
And we explained it as a case where the borrower admits,
and the reason is: perhaps he wrote it to borrow in ניסן
but he did not actually borrow until תשרי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge from the גיטין משנה was answered, the גמרא opens a new challenge against אביי from our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that the witnesses' signatures acquire for the lender
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה worries about an early date, but that worry seems to depend on the document having no power before the loan.

steps.title: Fits רב אסי but seems to contradict אביי
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי can say the משנה is talking about ordinary documents, so the early-date worry makes sense. But according to אביי, the witnesses already acquired the lien from the date written, so why worry?
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits רב אסי, who says writing without the lender is allowed only with transfer documents. He can say the משנה is about documents that are not transfer documents, as we explained. But according to אביי, who says the witnesses acquire for the lender through their signatures, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the question. The משנה fits רב אסי, but it seems to contradict אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the lien starts when the witnesses sign, even before any money is given. So a document dated ניסן truly gives a lien from ניסן, and an early date is not a real problem. If so, why should the found document not be returned?

keyTerms.meaning: This fits well with one view, but not with the other view coming next
Transfer documents, where the borrower formally sells a lien on his land
Its witnesses acquire for him through their signatures
What is there to say? This is how the גמרא asks a strong question

phrases.english: It works well according to רב אסי
who says it is only with transfer documents —
phrases.notes: He means that writing a document without the lender present is allowed only in this kind of document.

phrases.english: he can explain it as documents that are not transfer documents,
and it is as we said.
But according to אביי, who says:
its witnesses, by their signatures, acquire for him,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the actual challenge, using the משנה brought in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that the witnesses acquire the lien for the lender
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the witnesses' signatures already give a lien from the written date, an early date is not a problem. So the משנה's reason for not returning the document disappears.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה worries about repayment and a scheme
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה's reason is different. It worries the debt was already paid, and the two sides are working together to take land from buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי could tell you: this is the reason of the משנה. We worry that the debt was repaid and that there is a scheme.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by giving the משנה a different reason, one that has nothing to do with the date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the borrower admits the debt, maybe he already paid it. He and the lender could be using the old document together to take land from buyers and split the profit. This reason works even if the witnesses acquired the lien for the lender, so אביי's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He could tell you, meaning this is how he would answer
Repayment of the debt
A scheme, where the borrower and lender work together to cheat buyers
We worry about it, so we take it into account

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with the earlier worry. The earlier reason was an early date. This new reason is that the debt may already be paid, and the borrower's admission may be part of a plan.

phrases.english: אביי could tell you:
this is the reason of the משנה:
because we worry about repayment and a scheme.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, making it 'we worry.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the משנה a different reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה's only reason was a document dated earlier than the loan.
steps.terutzMaskana: For אביי, the משנה is worried about repayment and a scheme, which works with his view.

steps.title: What would שמואל say about the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל does not worry about repayment and a scheme, so he cannot use אביי's answer. If he holds like רב אסי, it works. If he holds like אביי, the question is back.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to שמואל, who says we do not worry about repayment and a scheme, what can we say? It is fine if he holds like רב אסי, who says it is only with transfer documents. Then he can say the משנה is about documents that are not transfer documents. But if he holds like אביי, who says the witnesses acquire for the lender through their signatures, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. אביי's answer cannot work for שמואל, so how does שמואל explain the משנה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not accept the repayment-and-scheme reason, so he needs the early-date reason. That reason works only with רב אסי's approach. If שמואל holds like אביי, he seems to have no reason left for the משנה. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine, meaning this works out according to this view
He holds like, meaning he agrees with that opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that each answer to the משנה depends on a set of views. Whoever does not worry about repayment and a scheme needs the early-date reason, which seems to conflict with אביי.

phrases.english: And according to שמואל, who says
we do not worry about repayment and a scheme,
what is there to say?

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב אַסִּי
phrases.english: It is fine if he holds like רב אסי
who says it is only with transfer documents —
he can explain the משנה as documents that are not transfer documents.
But if he holds like אביי
who says its witnesses, by their signatures, acquire for him,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר לָא חָיְישִׁינַן לְפֵרָעוֹן וְלִקְנוּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that אביי's answer in step 11 cannot work for שמואל, so the question returns.
steps.kashyaTarget: How שמואל explains the משנה if he holds like אביי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל does not accept the repayment-and-scheme reason. The early-date reason does not fit אביי's view. So if שמואל holds like אביי, he has no reason for the משנה.

steps.title: שמואל reads the משנה as a borrower who denies the debt
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה's case is one where the borrower does not admit he owes the money. That is why the documents are not returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל sets up our משנה as a case where the borrower does not admit the debt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 12 by giving שמואל a different setting for the משנה. The borrower denies the debt, so the found document is not handed to the lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not need to worry about an early date or a repayment scheme. In his reading, the משנה says 'do not return' simply because the borrower is denying the loan. Handing over the document would let the lender collect over the borrower's denial.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets up, explains a source as talking about a specific case
The one who owes; here, the borrower
Admits

phrases.english: Shmuel sets up our Mishnah
as a case where the borrower does not admit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised for שמואל in step 12 by placing the משנה in a new case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-setting the case of the משנה (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed stuck, because he does not use the repayment-scheme worry, and if he holds like אביי the early-date worry is gone too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a borrower who denies the debt, so the reason not to return is his denial itself.

steps.title: Then why return a document with no property guarantee?
steps.stepSummary: If the borrower denies the debt, even a document with no property guarantee should not be returned. The lender could still collect from the borrower's own unsold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, when the documents have no property guarantee, why return them? True, the lender cannot collect from sold property, but he can collect from the borrower's free property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading. The משנה says documents without a property guarantee are returned, but with a denying borrower, that seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document without a property guarantee cannot take land from buyers. Still, it should be good against property the borrower still owns. So returning it would hurt a borrower who says he does not owe anything.

keyTerms.meaning: A property guarantee written in the document, which ties the borrower's land to the loan
Liened property that was already sold to buyers
Free property that the borrower still owns
Granted, true

phrases.english: If so,
when they do not have a property guarantee,
why should he return them?
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the משנה, which says documents without a guarantee are returned.

phrases.english: Granted, he cannot collect from sold, liened property,
but from free property he can surely collect!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כִּי אֵין בָּהֶן אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים אַמַּאי יַחְזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading of the משנה as a borrower who denies the debt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the borrower denies, returning any document that can still collect hurts him. A document without a guarantee can still collect from free property, so it should not be returned. Yet the משנה says it is returned.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי מאיר: no guarantee means no collecting at all
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds like רבי מאיר, who says a loan document without a property guarantee collects from nothing, not even free property. So returning it does the borrower no harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל follows his own view. For שמואל said that רבי מאיר used to say: a loan document without a property guarantee collects neither from sold property nor from free property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by showing that שמואל holds a document without a guarantee cannot collect anything at all. So the lender gains nothing against the borrower by getting it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in step 14 assumed such a document still collects from free property. שמואל, quoting רבי מאיר, denies that. With no power to collect, giving it back cannot hurt the denying borrower.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his known view
A loan document
Collects the debt

phrases.english: Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for Shmuel said,
Rabbi Meir used to say:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁטַר חוֹב שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים –
phrases.english: a loan document that has no property guarantee
does not collect, not from sold, liened property
and not from free property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14 by bringing שמואל's own known view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Consistency with the speaker's own known view (לטעמיה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A document without a guarantee can still collect from the borrower's free property, so returning it would hurt the borrower.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to שמואל in the name of רבי מאיר, such a document collects nothing at all, so returning it is harmless.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how שמואל can keep his reading of the משנה, as a borrower who denies the debt, without contradicting the משנה's ruling on documents with no guarantee.

steps.title: If it collects nothing, why return it at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the document has no power to collect, what is the point of returning it to the lender?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since he cannot collect with it, why should the finder return it?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer in step 15 creates a new puzzle. If the document is useless for collecting, why does the משנה bother saying it should be returned?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Returning a lost object normally means giving back something of value to its owner. If the document cannot collect anything, it seems to have no value. Then the ruling 'return it' looks pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, seeing that
He should return it

phrases.english: But since he cannot collect with it,
why should the finder return it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה אַמַּאי יַחְזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in step 15 and questions what is left of the משנה's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling to return documents without a guarantee, as read through שמואל and רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A document that collects nothing has no value. So there seems to be no reason to bother returning it.

steps.title: It is returned as plain paper to cover a flask
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן בר אושעיא answers that the lender can use the document as a piece of paper to cover the mouth of his flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן בר אושעיא said: it is returned so the lender can use it to cover the mouth of his flask.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן בר אושעיא answers the last question. The document is still the lender's paper, and paper has a simple everyday use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The document's value is not as a legal tool but as a piece of paper. Even that small value belongs to its owner, so the finder must return it. The next step challenges this answer: why should the paper go to the lender and not the borrower?

keyTerms.meaning: To wrap, to tie over
A small flask or bottle
The lender

steps.whatToRemember: For שמואל: the משנה speaks of a borrower who denies the debt. A document with a property guarantee is not returned, because it could be used to collect against his denial. A document without a guarantee is returned, because, following רבי מאיר, it collects nothing. It is just the lender's paper, useful to cover a flask.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the lender can collect anything with this returned document. In this explanation it is returned only as a plain piece of paper.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan bar Oshaya said:
to wrap over the mouth of his flask,
the lender's flask.
phrases.notes: He means the paper has an ordinary use, like a lid, even though it has no legal power.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא: לָצוֹר עַל פִּי צְלוֹחִיתוֹ שֶׁל מַלְוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16. Step 18 then challenges this answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a small remaining value of the object
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A document that cannot collect has no value, so returning it is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: It still has value as paper, for example to cover the lender's flask, so it must be returned to him.

steps.title: Why not give the paper to the borrower?
steps.stepSummary: If the document is worth only its paper, it could just as easily go to the לוה to cover his own flask.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the finder give it back to the borrower, so the borrower can cover the opening of his own flask!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי נתן בר אושעיא's answer. If the document is just a scrap of paper, why does it go to the מלוה and not to the לוה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the lender gets the document only to use the paper as a flask cover. But once the document has no legal power, the lender has no special claim to it. The borrower could use the paper just as well, so why should the lender get it?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him return it
The borrower
The lender
A small flask or jug

phrases.english: Then let him return it to the borrower
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, the finder is the one returning it.

phrases.aramaic: לָצוֹר עַל פִּי צְלוֹחִיתוֹ שֶׁל לֹוֶה!
phrases.english: to cover the opening of the borrower's flask!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 17 that the lender gets it as paper for his flask.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי נתן בר אושעיא's claim that the document goes to the lender as a flask cover.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the document is only paper, the lender has no stronger claim to it than the borrower, so it could just as well go to the borrower.

steps.title: The answer begins with the borrower
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer by pointing to the לוה himself. The rest of the answer continues on the next עמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer to the challenge in Step 18. Only the opening words are here, and the full answer continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer opens with 'the borrower is,' which shows the reason will be based on the borrower himself. We have to wait for the next words to learn exactly what the borrower says or wants.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the borrower (who...)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer is not complete yet. Do not try to finish it from these two words; it continues on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: It is the borrower

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The answer explains the outcome from the borrower's own position, and it continues past this point.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the paper is useless, it could just as well go to the borrower.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer is still in progress. It begins by pointing to the borrower, and the reason follows.
